from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The One-Way Street (Hashing)", [
            "Cryptographic hashes create unique digital fingerprints.",
            "The process is strictly a one-way street.",
            "Input data is transformed into a fixed digest.",
            "Reversing the operation is mathematically impossible.",
            "Think of it as a permanent blender effect."
        ])

        # Objects
        title = Text("Hashing: One-way function", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(title, 'A2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        input_data = Text("data", font_size=48, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(input_data, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        blender = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE)
        blender_label = Text("Hash", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        blender_label.move_to(blender.get_center())
        blender_group = VGroup(blender, blender_label)
        self.place_at_grid(blender_group, 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        hash_digest = Text("f7a8...91b2", font_size=48, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(hash_digest, 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(title))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(blender_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(FadeIn(input_data))
        self.play(input_data.animate.move_to(self.grid['C4']), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeOut(input_data), FadeIn(hash_digest))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Proof of Work validates network activity.",
            "Miners guess nonces for specific hash results.",
            "This trial and error requires immense effort."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Digital Puzzle: Proof of Work", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        pow_text = Text("Proof of Work", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(pow_text, 'B3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(pow_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        nonce_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        nonce_text = always_redraw(lambda: Text(f"Nonce: {int(nonce_tracker.get_value())}", color="#FF0000"))
        self.place_at_grid(nonce_text, 'D3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.add(nonce_text)
        self.play(nonce_tracker.animate.set_value(999), run_time=2)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        valid_hash = Text("Hash: 0000a1b2...", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(valid_hash, 'E3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Write(valid_hash))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Chaining the Blocks", ["Blocks chain together via previous hashes.", "This creates an immutable chronological history.", "Altering one link invalidates the entire chain."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in #FFFFFF text 'Block Chaining'.
        chaining_text = Text("Block Chaining", color=WHITE, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(chaining_text, "A3")
        self.play(FadeIn(chaining_text))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show Block A #FF0000 linking to Block B.
        block_a = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=0.5)
        block_b = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(block_a, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(block_b, "C5")
        
        link_line = Line(block_a.get_right(), block_b.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(Create(block_a), Create(block_b), Create(link_line))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw #00FF00 pointer from Block B to Block A hash.
        pointer = Arrow(start=block_b.get_bottom(), end=block_a.get_bottom() + DOWN*0.5, color="#00FF00")
        hash_label = Text("Hash A", color="#00FF00", font_size=20)
        hash_label.next_to(pointer, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(pointer), Write(hash_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Hashing, Proof-of-Work, and ECC form Bitcoin.",
            "These primitives enable decentralized trust systems.",
            "The network acts as a global ledger."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        bitcoin_title = Text("Bitcoin Mechanics", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(bitcoin_title, "B2")
        self.play(FadeIn(bitcoin_title))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        blockchain = VGroup()
        for i in range(4):
            block = Square(side_length=0.6, color="#00FF00")
            block.next_to(blockchain, RIGHT, buff=0.1) if len(blockchain) > 0 else block.move_to(self.grid["D2"])
            blockchain.add(block)
        
        self.play(Create(blockchain))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        final_block = blockchain[-1]
        self.play(final_block.animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.wait(2)

outline.target_audience: University students with a basic interest in computer science and mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The One-Way Street (Hashing)
sections.content: Introduce cryptographic hash functions (SHA-256). Explain that they are 'one-way'—easy to compute forward, impossible to reverse. Visualize this as a 'digital fingerprint' generator.
sections.example: Imagine a blender: putting in a strawberry makes a unique smoothie, but you can never turn the smoothie back into a strawberry.

sections.title: The Digital Puzzle: Proof of Work
sections.content: Explain the mining process. Computers must find a 'nonce' that, when combined with transaction data, produces a hash starting with a specific number of zeros. This is a game of trial and error.
sections.example: A group of robots guessing a combination lock code. As the difficulty increases, the lock requires more digits to be correct, making it exponentially harder to guess.

sections.title: Chaining the Blocks
sections.content: Describe the blockchain data structure. Each block contains the hash of the *previous* block. This creates an unbreakable chronological link. If you change one transaction, the subsequent hashes become invalid.
sections.example: A series of glass boxes where each box contains a key to the next. If you break into the first box, the connection to all subsequent boxes snaps instantly, alerting everyone.

sections.title: Ownership: Elliptic Curve Cryptography
sections.content: Explain how private and public keys work. Based on the discrete logarithm problem, it is easy to derive a public key from a private key, but impossible to do the reverse.
sections.example: A magical 'stamp' (private key) that can only be used by its owner to sign a document, while the world uses a 'public sensor' to verify that the stamp belongs to you without ever seeing the stamp itself.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Connect these pieces: Hashing secures the data, Proof-of-Work prevents tampering, and Elliptic Curves provide identity. Together, they create a decentralized trust system.
sections.example: Visualize the entire network as a digital beehive where every bee (node) keeps a perfect record, and changing one cell requires the effort of the entire colony.
